001: Have you thought about which direction you want to take your career in the coming years?
I have, but I admit I'm still torn between staying in the technical field or moving into management.
And what has weighed the most on this decision so far?
The desire to have more impact on strategic decisions, but also the fear of losing touch with the hands-on work.
That's a very common concern for people at a senior level.
Right, that's why I've been trying to talk to people who have already made that transition to understand it better.
002: I attended a workshop on leadership yesterday, and it made me reflect a lot on my role.
That's great! What did you find most interesting in what was presented?
The idea that leadership isn't a position, but an attitude that we develop in our day-to-day.
I agree with that point. I think a lot of people wait to get promoted to only then start acting like a leader.
Exactly, and the workshop showed that you can practice it right away, even without having anyone reporting to you.
That makes total sense. I'll even look for materials on this topic to go deeper into it too.
003: Have you thought about asking for more structured feedback from your manager?
I have, but I admit I feel a bit insecure about how to start that conversation.
A good way is to ask for concrete examples of situations where you did well and where you can improve.
That really helps, because vague feedback ends up not generating any action plan.
And after receiving it, it's worth writing everything down and creating clear goals for the coming months.
Great idea. I'll schedule a meeting with him this week and already bring these questions ready.
004: I noticed you've been really interested in data and analysis. Have you thought about specializing in that?
I have been thinking about it, but I'm unsure if it's worth investing in a long course right now.
Maybe you don't need a full course right off the bat. A shorter, more focused program could already give you a solid foundation.
That's true, and the market has really valued people who combine business vision with that analytical side.
Without a doubt. And your current experience already gives you a huge edge in that sense.
Thanks for the encouragement. I'll research good options and put together a development plan for next semester.
005: Have you considered seeking mentorship within the company?
I've thought about it, but I don't know exactly how to approach a more senior person to make that request.
A natural approach is to ask for a quick chat to learn about their career path and ask for advice.
And after that first contact, how would I maintain the mentoring relationship?
You can propose monthly meetings and always bring concrete questions to make good use of the time.
That makes sense. I think I was overestimating the formality of this process; it doesn't need to be so bureaucratic.
006: Have you been keeping an eye on the internal job openings that come up at the company?
I do, but I still don't feel ready to apply for a leadership position.
Why do you think you're not ready? A lot of times we underestimate ourselves.
I think I lack more experience in people management and in handling difficult conversations.
But those skills can be developed little by little, even in smaller projects.
That's a good point. Maybe I could start by leading a volunteer initiative within the team to build up my confidence.
007: Have you thought about building a stronger personal brand outside the company?
I've thought about it, but I always end up putting it off because my daily routine ends up taking up all my time.
I understand, but even one hour a week already makes a difference for sharing what you learn.
Where do you suggest I start? I'm torn between writing articles or recording short videos.
It depends on your style, but writing about your field of work is a great start for organizing your ideas.
True, and it also helps solidify the knowledge. I'll try to publish something next month.
008: Have you talked to HR about the career possibilities in other areas of the company?
Not yet, but I'm curious to better understand how internal transitions work.
It's really worth scheduling that conversation, because they can show you paths you never even imagined.
Do you think I should already bring some kind of plan, or just go to learn about the options?
I think it's better to go with an open mind, but also with some questions about what you like to do.
Good tip. I'll schedule that conversation for next month and see what comes up.
009: Have you thought about how your current work contributes to the company's long-term goals?
I admit I've never stopped to think about that deeply; I just focus on what needs to be delivered.
Understanding that bigger impact can help you see where you add the most value.
And how could I figure that out? Should I ask my manager directly?
Yes, a good conversation about the team's priorities and how your role fits into them already clears up a lot.
I'll do that. I think this broader view will also help me better direct my own development.
010: Have you assessed whether your work-life balance is healthy at this stage of your career?
I admit I've been working too much, and that has been worrying me, but I'm afraid of missing out on opportunities.
That's a real risk, because burnout ends up taking a heavy toll down the road.
Do you have any suggestions on how to set boundaries without seeming less committed?
A good practice is to set clear hours and communicate your availability transparently with the team.
Thanks for the conversation. I'll rethink my routine to grow in a more sustainable way.
